clue.text: One set of good books pronounced worthy — that's understandable

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Good Book

indicators.note: pronounced says the next word is to be heard rather than read as spelt

parts.note: worthy means eligible, fit to be chosen

explanation.surface: Someone praises a collection of improving books as worthy and therefore easy to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' means the last part only sounds like ELIGIBLE; it is written ELLIGIBLE to finish the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intelligible can be understood, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Kind of motor, note, used in radio broadcast

indicators.note: used in says the note is placed inside the other letters
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of radio are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
NB, nota bene, is a written note meaning 'mark well'

explanation.surface: A motor of some kind gets a mention during a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is not a musical note here but the written reminder NB; 'broadcast' scatters RADIO to IOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: An inboard motor is an engine mounted inside a boat's hull, one kind of motor.

clue.text: Imperial assembly — strictly for the birds?

definitions.meaning: ... was the 1521 assembly of the Holy Roman Empire that tried Luther
read literally, a bird's diet consists of worms

explanation.definitionFit: The famous Diet at the German city of Worms was an imperial assembly; read literally it is what birds eat.

clue.text: Trenet song that's less effective

definitions.meaning: ... is the famous song by French singer Charles Trenet
the comparative of lame, weak or unconvincing

explanation.definitionFit: La Mer is Charles Trenet's best-known song, and a lamer excuse is a weaker, less effective one.

clue.text: One who makes demands to popular nurse

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sister is a senior nurse in British hospitals

explanation.surface: Someone pressing demands upon a well-liked nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists is a person pressing demands, an agent-noun synonym.

clue.text: Irritation that can hurt, from the first

definitions.text: Irritation that can hurt, from the first

indicators.note: from the first says to take the opening letter of each word of the clue

explanation.surface: An irritation that has been painful from the very beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the initials of its first four words spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a skin irritation, and scratching it can hurt.

clue.text: Poet's getting money, with case overturned

parts.note: lucre is money, often filthy lucre

indicators.note: overturned means the word for case is turned upside down in this down clue

parts.note: a suit is a case in law

explanation.surface: A poet comes into money while a lawsuit against him is overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' is 'Poet is', with 'getting' and 'with' as links; 'case' is a lawsuit, and 'overturned' reverses it to ITUS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucretius was the Roman poet who wrote De Rerum Natura.

clue.text: Treasure-seeker pants hugely, having diseased liver

parts.note: long johns are underpants with very long legs, pants on a huge scale

indicators.note: diseased signals that the organ's letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A treasure hunter breathes heavily because he has a sick liver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like a verb (breathes hard) but is the noun for underwear; 'diseased' turns LIVER into ILVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the pirate who hunts the treasure in Stevenson's Treasure Island.

clue.text: Danger —— English leaving for that reason

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for English goes out of the longer word

parts.note: thereat is an old word meaning for that reason

explanation.surface: Danger looms, which is why the English are departing.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a source of danger, a close synonym.

clue.text: Fish -— ray circling river

indicators.note: circling means the word for ray goes round the river letter

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: A fish, a ray, swimming round in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' looks like another fish but means a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream is a freshwater fish, an example of the class.

clue.text: Fire the clergy as part of repentance

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Dismissing the priesthood as an act of penance.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing sackcloth and ashes is the traditional outward sign of penitence.

clue.text: A good craftsman who wastes some time but gets a buzz out of his work

definitions.text: gets a buzz out of his work

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good

indicators.note: wastes says the time letter is lost from the craftsman word

parts.note: an artist is a skilled craftsman
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A conscientious craftsman who idles a little yet loves his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets a buzz' plays on the bees a beekeeper works with.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper works among buzzing bees, so his work literally gives him a buzz.

clue.text: The French fit into a sporting group

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
an ague is a fit of shivering or fever

explanation.surface: The French slot into a sports association.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is a group of sports teams competing together.

clue.text: Was hesitant at that point, having fiddled about

indicators.note: about means the cheating word goes round the place word

parts.note: did means cheated or swindled, as in 'I was done'
there means at that point or place

explanation.surface: Someone stalled at that moment, having messed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' suggests playing about, but DID here is slang for cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to be indecisive, so dithered means was hesitant.

clue.text: Take out one man wrongly found among the most gifted

indicators.note: found among means the scrambled piece sits inside the gifted group

parts.note: the elite are the most talented people

indicators.note: wrongly signals the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Remove one man discovered by mistake in the top group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges the letters of 'one man' (I plus MAN) into MINA.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to remove or knock out, matching take out.

clue.text: Animal not allowed in gorge

parts.note: a pig is an animal
out means ruled out, not permitted

explanation.surface: A banned animal found in a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a ravine but is the verb meaning to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig out is informal for gorging oneself on food.

clue.text: Laid down the law if raid done improperly

indicators.note: improperly signals the letters are arranged wrongly

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruling was laid down after a raid was badly carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordained means decreed by authority, laying down the law.

clue.text: Pastry's warmer at home

parts.note: a muff is a fur tube for keeping hands warm
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone's pastry is the warm one they keep in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffin is a baked item from the bakery, loosely a pastry.

clue.text: Female graduate making a complaint

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A woman with a degree lodging a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grievance but means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an ailment, which is a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: One is inside more likely

indicators.note: inside means the little word goes within the comparative

parts.note: proner means more inclined or more likely
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who's already locked up is more likely to offend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is British slang for in prison, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'inside' is slang for being in jail, so one who is inside is a convict.

clue.text: Take over from old magistrate, accepting half of lies

indicators.note: accepting means the magistrate word takes the letters in

parts.note: a reeve was a local magistrate in medieval England

indicators.note: half of means only the first two of the four letters are used

explanation.surface: Replace a former official who tolerates some untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: A reeve was an English local official; 'half of' picks LI from 'lies'.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to take over their duty or shift.

clue.text: Small meteor makes loud noise, back behind house

indicators.note: behind places the reversed noise after the house

parts.note: Leo is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac

indicators.note: back means the noise word is read in reverse

parts.note: din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A small shooting star makes a racket at the back of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The zodiac signs are called houses in astrology; 'back' turns the racket word into NID.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leonids are a November meteor shower; a single small meteor of it is a Leonid.

clue.text: Primate gets servant to exercise

parts.note: a man is a manservant
drill is repetitive exercise or training

explanation.surface: A senior churchman gets his butler to work out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, but it is the monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrill is a large West African monkey, an example of a primate.

clue.text: European network sent up a sad song

indicators.note: sent up means the pieces are written bottom to top in this down entry

parts.note: a grid is a network, such as the power network

explanation.surface: A European network broadcast a mournful number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns EGRID into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song, often a funeral lament.

clue.text: German produces extravagant Ring

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extravagant
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A German stages a lavish Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests Wagner's operas but just gives the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's name, so a German.

clue.text: Foolish paintings showing Scottish town

parts.note: dumb means stupid or foolish
art means paintings collectively
on means being shown, as a play is on

explanation.surface: Silly pictures on display in a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbarton is a town on the Clyde in western Scotland.

clue.text: Show is for audience to see again

indicators.note: for audience means it is the spoken form that counts

parts.note: to review is to look at again

explanation.surface: A stage show is something a crowd wants to watch twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical show of sketches and songs.

clue.text: Burns might be the result of a thesis

definitions.meaning: burns are graded by severity, and middling burns that blister are given this middle grade
a master's award earned by writing a thesis is the next university qualification after a bachelor's

explanation.definitionFit: Burns of medium severity are classed by degree, and a master's earned by thesis follows a first university award.
